records.interpretation: 360 is the full donation; 15% is the fraction set aside; the unknown is a notebook count.

editorial_observations.note: 360 ÷ 15 uses the right whole but the wrong percent operation. It does not alone prove that another base was selected.

draft_diagnostic_prompts: Which amount represents the full donation?
Does 15% name a number of notebooks or a fraction of the full donation?
records.transfer_limit: Potential approved prerequisite assessment after review/approval; different context from sale-price tasks, but only direct percentage amount.

records.interpretation: 18 is the cycling part and 60 is the whole group of invitees; the unknown is a percentage.

editorial_observations.note: 60/18 = 3 1/3 is a ratio, not 3 1/3%. The foil requires inversion plus a missing percent conversion. Avoid describing it as a pure single-operation error.
70% is the non-cycling group. This is a target-group distinction; no ratio-sharing problem is involved.

draft_diagnostic_prompts: Which group is the whole when the question says percentage of invitees?
Does the question ask how many people cycled or what percentage cycled?
records.transfer_limit: Potential part/whole-to-rate application after approval; cannot assess reverse markup by itself.

records.interpretation: 72 is the encoded quarter, not the original total or the unencoded remainder.

methods: 25% is one quarter. Four quarters contain 4 × 72 = 288 files.

editorial_observations.note: Ask what 72 represents before claiming the learner selected a wrong base.
72/0.75 assumes 72 is the 75% remainder. Confirm that interpretation; the code alone loses the distinction.

draft_diagnostic_prompts: Does 72 represent all assigned files, the completed part, or the remaining part?
If 72 is one quarter, how many such equal quarters form the whole?
records.transfer_limit: Useful inverse-percent prerequisite after approval. It recovers a whole from a 25% part; it is a different relation from reversing a 25% markup, where the given final is 125%.

records.interpretation: ₱180 is already after the raise; the unknown original is 100% and the given final is 120%.

editorial_observations.note: 180 − 20 treats 20% as ₱20. Separate unit interpretation from reversing a multiplication.

draft_diagnostic_prompts: Has the 20% raise already happened when the allowance is ₱180?
Is ₱180 the original 100%, or the new 120% of the original?
records.transfer_limit: Closest existing reverse-raise near practice for the ₱640 contrast after approval. A 20% allowance raise is the same inverse-multiplier family as a 25% price markup, so it is not full unfamiliar-family transfer.
